content_ta: வரவிருக்கும் 2027 French ஜனாதிபதித் தேர்தலுக்கான சூதாட்ட முன்கணிப்புகளில் Le Pen 43.3% என்ற அளவிற்க்கு அருகில் இருப்பதாக சமீபத்திய Polymarket நிலவரம் காட்டுகிறது. இதற்கிடையில், அக்டோபர் 6 அன்று நடைபெற்ற பிரெஞ்சு பள்ளி மாணவர்களின் போராட்டங்களில் லட்சக்கணக்கானோர் பங்கேற்றனர். இத்தகைய நிகழ்வுகள் நாட்டில் அதிகரித்து வரும் அரசியல் மற்றும் சமூக பதட்டங்களை வெளிப்படுத்துகின்றன.

title: DSA White Paper Named Among the 2026 DC Fintech Week Winning Papers
summary: Washington, D.C., October 7, 2026 — The Digital Sovereignty Alliance (DSA), a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing clear and ethical public policy, research, and education related to emerging technologies, announced today that its white paper, “Modern Foundations of Personal Finance: Literacy and Infrastructure in the Digital Economy,” has been named one of five winning papers in DC Fintech Week’s 2026 Call for Papers and selected as 2026 Featured Research.   The paper was written by DSA Senior Policy Advisor Molly Woodman as lead author, with contributions from Adrian Wall, Managing Director; Emily Ekshian, Content Manager; and Maghan Lusk, Policy Associate.   Chosen from dozens of submissions, the winning papers are featured on the DC Fintech Week website at dcfintechweek.org and in the event’s announcement to its community. DC Fintech Week 2026 takes place October 13-16 in Washington, D.C.   The paper examines how the shift to digital financial systems is outpacing Americans’ financial literacy, with comprehension of risk the weakest area of knowledge. It also considers how gaps in understanding and access fall unevenly across households, and concludes that regulation and financial education must advance together.   “We’re grateful to DC Fintech Week for including our paper alongside such strong research,” said Molly Woodman, Senior Policy Advisor at DSA. “Most people are still getting comfortable with traditional finance, and now they’re being asked to make sense of digital assets too. Good rules can make these products safer, but they won’t help someone understand the risk they’re taking on. We hope this work encourages policymakers and educators to treat financial literacy as a priority along with regulation.”   The selection reflects DSA’s ongoing work to bring emerging technology expertise into policy discussions surrounding digital assets, financial infrastructure, consumer protection, and responsible innovation. Through research, education, and engagement with stakeholders across the public and private sectors, DSA works to advance policy frameworks that support innovation while prioritizing transparency, individual rights, and public welfare.   About the Digital Sovereignty Alliance The Digital Sovereignty Alliance (DSA) is a nonprofit social welfare organization committed to advocating for public policies that support ethical innovation in decentralized technologies, blockchain, cryptocurrency, Web3, and artificial intelligence. DSA conducts research, organizes educational events, and promotes policies that prioritize public welfare and digital sovereignty.   Media contact Maghan Lusk maghan.lusk@discoverdsa.org
content: The Digital Sovereignty Alliance announced that its white paper on digital finance and literacy has been named one of the winning papers for DC Fintech Week 2026. Authored by DSA team members, the research explores how digital financial systems are outpacing financial literacy in the United States and highlights the need for balanced regulation and education.
content_ta: Digital Sovereignty Alliance-ன் டிஜிட்டல் நிதி மற்றும் கல்வி தொடர்பான ஒயிட் பேப்பர், DC Fintech Week 2026-ன் வெற்றி பெற்ற ஆய்வுக் கட்டுரைகளில் ஒன்றாகத் தேர்ந்தெடுக்கப்பட்டுள்ளதாக அறிவிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. DSA குழுவினரால் எழுதப்பட்ட இந்த ஆய்வு, டிஜிட்டல் நிதி அமைப்புகள் நிதி கல்வியறிவை எவ்வாறு விஞ்சுகின்றன என்பதை ஆராய்கிறது மற்றும் சீரான ஒழுங்குமுறை மற்றும் கல்வியின் அவசியத்தை வலியுறுத்துகிறது.

title: Why Is ADA’s Price Down 8% Today Even as Cardano Whales Wake Up?
summary: ADA is down the most today among the larger-cap alts.
content: Cardano's native token ADA experienced an 8% price drop today, making it the worst performer among large-capitalization alternative cryptocurrencies. This decline occurred despite notable activity from large holders, commonly referred to as whales, who have recently become active in the market. The reasons behind this downward price movement amidst increased whale participation remain a point of interest for traders.
content_ta: Cardano-வின் சொந்த டோக்கனான ADA இன்று 8 சதவீதம் விலை குறைந்துள்ளது, இதனால் பெரிய சந்தை மூலதனம் கொண்ட மாற்று கிரிப்டோகரன்சிகளில் இதுவே அதிக சரிவை சந்தித்தது. 'வேல்ஸ்' என்று அழைக்கப்படும் பெரிய முதலீட்டாளர்களின் குறிப்பிடத்தக்க செயல்பாடுகள் இருந்தபோதிலும் இந்த விலை சரிவு ஏற்பட்டுள்ளது. அதிகரித்த முதலீட்டாளர் பங்கேற்புக்கு மத்தியில் இந்த விலை சரிவுக்கான காரணங்கள் வர்த்தகர்கள் மத்தியில் விவாதப் பொருளாக உள்ளது.

title: These Altcoins Bleed the Most After Bitcoin’s Sudden Drop Below $84K: Market Watch

content: Following a sudden drop in Bitcoin below $84,000, several major altcoins experienced significant losses across the cryptocurrency market. Tokens such as MNT, DOT, and UNI led the downward trend as the market reacted sharply to the price movement.

content_ta: Shiba Inu நீண்ட கால ஸ்பாட் மார்க்கெட் வர்த்தகத்தில் 440 சதவீத குறிப்பிடத்தக்க அதிகரிப்பைப் பதிவு செய்துள்ளது. இருப்பினும், குறுகிய கால ஆதரவு கணிசமாகக் குறைந்துள்ளதால் SHIB-ன் தற்போதைய நிலவரம் கவலை அளிக்கும் வகையில் உள்ளது.

content_ta: XRP ஹோல்டர்கள் மற்றும் முதலீட்டாளர்கள் மேலும் சில காலம் காத்திருக்க வேண்டியுள்ளது, ஏனெனில் XRP சொத்து நிறுவனத்தின் அதிகம் எதிர்பார்க்கப்பட்ட Nasdaq பட்டியலிடுதல் அதிகாரப்பூர்வமாக ஒத்திவைக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. திங்கட்கிழமை, அக்டோபர் 12 வரை வர்த்தகம் தற்காலிகமாக நிறுத்தப்பட்டுள்ளது, இதனால் நிறுவனத்தின் திட்டமிடப்பட்ட அறிமுகம் தாமதமாகிறது.

content_ta: Bitcoin தனது கடுமையான அக்டோபர் மாத வீழ்ச்சியின் ஆண்டு நிறைவை நெருங்கி வரும் வேளையில், அதன் சாதனையான உச்ச விலையை விட மிகக் குறைந்த விலையில் வர்த்தகம் செய்யப்படுகிறது. சந்தையானது கடந்த கால சரிவுகளைத் திரும்பிப் பார்க்கும் அதே வேளையில், டீசல் தட்டுப்பாடு குறித்த புதிய கவலைகள் உலகளாவிய சந்தைகளுக்கு கூடுதல் அச்சுறுத்தலாக உருவெடுத்துள்ளன. கிரிப்டோகரன்சி சந்தையின் இந்த வரலாற்று ரீதியான நிலையற்ற காலகட்டத்தில் முதலீட்டாளர்கள் நிலைமையை உன்னிப்பாகக் கவனித்து வருகின்றனர்.

title: Sui and Alibaba Want AI Agents to Spend Without Human Approval

Updated on the 7th of each month, Qonto Insights turns anonymized, aggregated transaction data from Qonto’s business customers in France, Germany, Italy, and Spain into evidence-based signals on the European SME economy. 
Whether cash flow pressure, payment delays, AI adoption, or international expansion, Qonto Insights is built to offer decision-makers, analysts, policymakers, and the media the earliest possible read on European business dynamics, drawn from the latest SME behavior and offered without interpretation or commentary. 
The platform is free to access from Qonto’s website and updated monthly, made up of four defined indexes on four distinct, key themes. 
The backbone of the EU economy has always been overlooked 
SMEs’ impact is everywhere in the European economy. Small businesses account for more than 30 million enterprises and make up 99% of all regional businesses, underpinning more than 100 million positions, and representing two-thirds of jobs in Europe. 
But true, on-the-ground understanding of their lived experience is lacking. With Qonto’s unique vantage point, counting 750,000+ SME customers across the continent, it is the business banking partner best-placed to offer a clear understanding of EU SMEs. 
Four indexes revealing the reality of EU SME life 
The platform’s four indexes each cover a different business health-related topic: 
- Cash Buffer Index: assesses how many days of cash buffer a typical business holds, the proportion of SMEs with at least a month's cash reserves, and how many dip into negative balance at some point during the month. 
- AI Adoption Index: shows how many European SMEs are investing in AI, how much is being spent on AI tools, and how many AI tools the typical business subscribes to. - Late Payments Index: looks at how many invoices are paid late, how long businesses wait for payments, and the average value of outstanding invoices. 
- International Transactions Index: maps how many European SMEs are doing business across borders, where they do business, and the average amount of money crossing borders.
And for more in-depth explorations, further analysis will be available in dedicated “Qonto Insights: Explained,” also on the Qonto Insights platform. These ad hoc round-ups will spotlight the notable findings from each country, compare market behaviors, and offer themed overviews on each index subject. 
The latest data, offered without interpretation 
Qonto Insights doesn’t add its own angle to the findings, meaning data that’s available quickly, with the latest insights only ever a maximum of one month old. 
Rather than spending weeks or months building full reports and analysis, Qonto Insights sees its in-house business intelligence teams simply pull, aggregate, and fully anonymize the figures before publishing them; letting journalists, policy-makers and other interested parties draw their own conclusions based on insights rather than instinct alone. 
Anonymized, aggregated data 
As with Qonto’s product, customer data safety is paramount. All figures on Qonto Insights pass through rigorous anonymity and aggregation checks, never citing any raw data. Instead the platform brings together findings using percentages, averages, and medians, to identify patterns in behavior. The bottom line: no data can be traced back to an individual customer. 
September’s data: improved cash reserves, a boost for AI adoption, more international business, but more invoices paid late 
In September’s inaugural Qonto Insights, a snapshot of the data shows: 
- Cash Buffer: EU SMEs held a median of 18.5 days’ cash runway (the amount needed to keep their business running, should they stop earning) - a small improvement of - 0.4 days vs. August. France was the clear frontrunner in cash reserves; their median stood at 19.4 days’ cash reserves (an EU high), in contrast with Italy’s 9.5 days (an EU low). Europe-wide, 7.4% dipped into negative balance at least once in the month - an improvement of -0.2% vs. August. 
- AI Adoption: 16.7% of small businesses used Qonto to pay for at least one AI subscription, up from 10% at the beginning of this year. AI spend is also rising - in September, SMEs paid on average €34.46 on AI tools. That’s a full €8.02 increase on the previous month alone. 
- Late Payments: 31.6% of invoices paid in September were paid late (reaching an EU high in Spain at 38.9%), with an average delay of 58.6 days - up 10.8 days from August. Yet, the average individual value of September’s late-paid invoices dropped to €3.9k apiece. 
- International Transactions: 20.6% of EU SMEs did international business in September - rising to an EU high of 23.5% in Germany - with transactions made between 154 countries. Businesses with 10+ employees were the most internationally active, with 35.1% making or receiving cross-border payments. 
"Qonto is in a fortunate position - we have a direct line to 750,000+ small businesses across eight European markets. Now, with Qonto Insights, we’re putting that enviable position to even more good use, shining a light on the situation on the ground for Europe’s small businesses." says Alexandre Prot, Co-Founder and CEO at Qonto. “From exposing the rate of late invoice payments to tracking the use of AI or international growth, it’s about putting real-time, real-world data behind hunches and hypotheticals, with trends that are updated every month. Qonto Insights gives everyone from journalists to policy-makers a front-row seat to the lived experience of small businesses - the EU’s economic backbone - through behavior-based data that’s true to life and more timely than ever.” 
Visit Qonto Insights at: www.qonto.com/en/insights

title: Noah Closes $38M Seed Funding Round as Major Enterprises Move Cross-Border Payments onto Stablecoin
summary:
Noah, the stablecoin payments infrastructure provider, has closed its seed funding round at $38 million following the raise of an additional $16 million from existing and new investors.  The raise follows strong growth that has seen revenues surge by 538% during year-to-date 2026 compared to the same period 2025, with recurring monthly growth of 31%.  Noah has also signed over 150 new customers during 2026 including major enterprises such as they transition to stablecoin transfers.  

The new funding will enable Noah to expand and accelerate its international money transfer services that enable the frictionless movement of funds across borders in seconds.  Specific application of the funds will be to expand Noah’s regulatory footprint, recruit engineering and compliance specialists, and deepen its connections with local payment rails in its highest-volume markets. The business will also now be able to accelerate its US expansion through opening an office in New York.  
“Stablecoins combine the flexibility of digital currencies with the stability of fiat currencies to allow money to move at the speed of the internet.  We are able to replace the slow and expensive traditional banking approach to international transfers with a single settlement platform,” said Shah Ramezani, Co-Founder and CEO of Noah. “Noah is building the infrastructure that will make one-click international transactions possible everywhere, with full compliance at both the origination and destination of funds. Just as neobanks have revolutionised domestic banking, we want to redefine global money transfer markets.” 
The new investment round has been made by Endeit Capital, FJ Labs, LocalGlobe, Felix Capital and a select group of high-profile angels.  The capital raise follows strong sector growth for stablecoin as well as revenue growth for Noah as customers replace legacy correspondent banking with faster and cheaper stablecoin transfers. 
Jonne de Leeuw, Partner at Endeit Capital in charge of the fund's fintech investments, said: "Cross-border payments still run on rails built decades ago, and we had been looking for the leader in stablecoin infrastructure for some time. We found it in Noah: the team and product are setting the standard in the space, and the customer traction shows the demand is real. Backing Thijn and Shah was a no-brainer, and we can't wait to see them take Noah to the next level." 
 

 
Stablecoin adoption within the SMB market is rapidly accelerating. B2B stablecoin payments have reached an annualised value of $226 billion, representing an increase of 733% year-over-year. Stablecoins today account for less than 1% of the $34.8 trillion in annual cross-border B2B payments, highlighting the opportunity for future adoption.  
Noah Co-Founder Thijn Lamers, who was also part of the founding team at global payment giant Adyen, said: "Stablecoin is critical to the future of money movement.  International transfers are highly regulated and increasingly challenging as every country, currency, and payment method requires local partnerships, integrations, and compliance infrastructure. We founded Noah to set money free by building an international network where the on-ramps, off-ramps and compliance are built in, so that payments can move seamlessly across the world.  
“Over the next 12 months, Noah is scaling its business to the level required to support four to five times its current revenue, with our longer term ambition to become the underlying network through which businesses move money internationally.  We want to make stablecoin settlement invisible to the companies and individuals benefiting from it,” added Lamers.  
Noah is live in more than 150 markets and supports over 60 currencies, where it enables seamless cross-border payments to replace legacy correspondent bank chains where multiple steps add delays and fees. Noah provides its services both directly to enterprises and individuals, and also indirectly through partnerships with consumer platforms, fintech companies, neobanks, and workforce platforms that aggregate large numbers of businesses, contractors, and individual users.

title: Black Friday Payments: Is the Retail Estate Ready for Peak?
summary:
On Black Friday last year, Barclays recorded card transactions 62% above its average day for 2025. Nationwide customers made a record 11.9 million transactions, at one point reaching 185 every second. For retailers, millions of those purchases depended on the payment infrastructure in stores: terminals on counters, handhelds on shop floors and kiosks by entrances.
Retailers plan stock, staffing and promotions months ahead of peak. The payments estate usually gets far less scrutiny, on the reasonable assumption that devices working in September will still be working in November…and most will. The trouble is that peak trading has a way of finding the weak points that were already there. That might be a terminal that occasionally drops its connection, a device running outdated software, or a spare that has sat in a drawer since 2023. Any of these is a minor irritation on an ordinary Tuesday. On the last Saturday before Christmas, with a queue to the door, it becomes a lost sale.
What an outage really costs
Research published in April by FreedomPay and Retail Economics estimated that payment failures put up to £1.7bn in UK retail and hospitality sales at risk each year. Businesses reported just over five major disruptions a year on average and 72% of them fell during peak trading windows. The average outage lasted 79 minutes, yet only 40% of businesses surveyed could take card payments offline. Very few shoppers will wait anywhere near that long. The same study found frustration typically sets in after around seven minutes.
Consumers are spending carefully this year and retailers will fight for every basket through pricing, promotions and marketing. Losing one of those sales at the final step is among the most avoidable losses of all.
Less slack in the system
Stores are also running with fewer people. UK retail employment fell to 2.75 million jobs in June, and the four-quarter average has dropped to its lowest level on record, according to the BRC. With employment costs still rising, simply adding more staff for peak is becoming a more expensive answer.
That changes what happens when a device fails. A member of staff used to be on hand to reboot it, fetch a replacement or ring the helpdesk while someone else kept the line moving. In a leaner store, that person is often busy elsewhere. Self-checkouts, kiosks and other unattended points of sale also have to keep serving customers without anyone permanently beside them. For grocers handling heavier Christmas baskets and higher footfall, one lane going down at the wrong moment can back up the entire store.
Five questions to ask now
None of this calls for alarm. It calls for an honest look at the estate while there is still time to act on what it shows. Five questions cover most of the ground.
How is every device performing today? Not how many terminals you own, but which are online, which fail most often and what software each one is running.
Where are your oldest devices? If they sit in your busiest stores, that's where any weakness could become most costly.
How much can you fix without a site visit? Pushing an update or reconfiguring devices overnight across hundreds of stores is very different from waiting for an engineer in mid-December.
Can you add checkout capacity quickly? Mobile terminals and SoftPOS on a standard smartphone can ease pressure at the tills, support concessions and serve pop-up trading without permanent hardware. Standards such as PCI MPoC have also strengthened the security framework around mobile acceptance, making SoftPOS a practical option for mainstream retail.
What happens when the network drops? Offline processing and failover connectivity are dull subjects right up until the moment they save a trading day.
Decided before the doors open
Much of the outcome of peak is settled before the first Black Friday queue forms. In our experience, readiness has less to do with having the newest kit than with knowing what you have, where it sits, how it is performing and how quickly you can respond when something slips.
That preparation is unglamorous: audits, updates, spares in the right places and support plans agreed in advance. With Black Friday weeks away, there is time to get it done.

title: Sumsub Launches Reusable KYC Gateway, Cutting Repeat Verification for MiniPay’s Network
summary:
Sumsub, the AI-powered trust infrastructure for compliance operations at scale, today launched Reusable KYC Gateway at Token2049 Singapore. MiniPay, one of the fastest growing stablecoin wallets, is the first live integrator, giving its users a shared verification experience across MiniPay's partner network. 
MiniPay users can verify their identity once and reuse it at every regulated partner in that network, without MiniPay needing to store, handle or control sensitive personal data like identity documents. Gateway is the newest addition to Sumsub's Reusable KYC product line, which also includes Reusable KYC Share.
Solving repeat verification at scale
MiniPay operates across more than 70 countries with over 20 million wallets opened to date. As a self-custodial wallet, MiniPay does not need to verify users itself. Each of its partners, including on and off ramps, card issuers and payment providers, has traditionally run its own separate KYC process. That means the same user re-uploads documents and resubmits a selfie every time they interact with a new partner, even though they are verifying the same identity inside the same ecosystem. Each repeat check is a fresh drop off point, costing partners conversion and costing users time.
One verification, every partner
Reusable KYC Gateway removes that repetition. Users verify once with Sumsub, then unlock each new regulated partner service in MiniPay's network with a single tap. When a MiniPay user is prompted to verify, they either draw on one of the 15 million pre-existing Sumsub IDs or complete a new check with an ID document and a selfie. The user explicitly consents to connect that verified identity to their MiniPay account, keeping control over what is shared and with whom.
From there, when the user first interacts with a regulated partner in MiniPay's network, they consent once to share their identity with that partner, and the partner receives the verified identity directly from Sumsub ID. The partner can then complete verification without any extra user screens while still running its own compliance checks against its policies, with additional checks required for higher-risk transactions.
As the verified identity is passed directly from Sumsub to the partner, MiniPay does not collect, store or handle sensitive identity documents or biometric data itself.
Results for MiniPay's partner network
Since adopting the approach, MiniPay partners have seen verification conversion rise from approximately 70% to 95%, and KYC completion time fall by up to 50%. Eight of MiniPay's partners already use Sumsub for verification.
"Repeated KYC checks across the same ecosystem are inconvenient for everyone, and one in three applicants we see have already verified with us before," said Andrew Novoselsky, Chief Product Officer at Sumsub. "Reusable KYC Gateway puts that reuse to work for MiniPay's users, giving them a single verified identity that works throughout its entire partner network, with full control over what they share and with whom."
“Self-custody has always been central to MiniPay. Users hold their own funds, and now they also control their own verified identity,“ said Murray Spark, Senior Director of Business Development at Opera. “They decide what to share and with whom, and that matters more and more as our partner network expands across new markets."

title: Octane Closes $1.4 Billion Forward-Flow Deal with New York Life, MetLife Investment Management, Equitable, Pacific Life, and Victory Park Capital
summary:
Octane® (Octane Lending, Inc.), the fintech unlocking the power of financial products for retailers and consumers, announced today that it has executed a $1.4 billion forward-flow facility, marking the Company's largest forward-flow transaction to date and further deepening its relationships with leading institutional investors.
New York Life Investment Management, the asset management business of New York Life, was the Loan Arranger and Lead Investor along with MetLife Investment Management, the institutional asset management business of MetLife, Inc. (NYSE: MET), Equitable, a leading financial services organization and principal franchise of Equitable Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: EQH), Pacific Life, and Victory Park Capital, a leading global alternative investment firm specializing in private credit. AB CarVal, an established global alternative investment manager and part of AllianceBernstein's Private Alternatives business, served as Investment Advisor to Equitable in connection with the transaction. Under the terms of the agreement, the parties have jointly agreed to purchase up to $1.4 billion backed by fixed-rate installment, full-spectrum powersports and outdoor power equipment loans originated by Octane's in-house lender, Roadrunner Financial, LLC. Octane's in-house loan servicer, Roadrunner Account Services, LLC, will service the loans.
This transaction marks Octane's third forward-flow partnership with funds managed by life insurance providers and builds on its existing relationships with New York Life, MetLife, and Equitable, each of which participated in the Company's $700 million forward-flow facility announced in April 2025.
"Our largest-ever forward-flow facility marks a significant milestone for Octane and our capital markets program," said Nicholas Makarov, SVP and Head of Capital Markets at Octane. "We're grateful to each of our partners for their continued confidence in our platform. The scale of this transaction and the quality of partners participating reflect the strength and consistency of our credit performance, the continued demand from leading institutional investors for Octane-originated assets, and our ability to build and deepen relationships with best-in-class capital partners."
"Building on our inaugural facility, we are proud to close a second forward-flow commitment with Octane alongside an expanded group of institutional partners," said Brendan Feeney, Managing Director and Head of Consumer Asset Based Finance, Private Fixed Income. Private Fixed Income is part of New York Life Investment Management (NYLIM), a global investment platform with approximately $837 billion assets under management, delivering tailored solutions across public and private markets. "This transaction reinforces NYLIM's commitment to sourcing high-quality, differentiated assets for our portfolio while supporting Octane's continued growth and market leadership."
With this transaction, Octane continues to expand its base of high-quality institutional capital partners. To date, the Company has sold or secured commitments to sell more than $6.3 billion of consumer loans through its forward-flow and whole-loan programs, including approximately $3.4 billion in commitments in 2026. The transaction further strengthens Octane's diversified capital markets platform, alongside an asset-backed securitization program that has issued more than $5 billion of notes to date, including its $337 million RV and Marine securitization, the Company's largest in the asset class to date.
The forward-flow announcement follows a period of continued growth and momentum for Octane. In the first half of 2026, Octane grew originations by 37% year-over-year and surpassed $9 billion in all-time originations. Octane also announced significant Captive-as-a-Service™ partnerships in the powersports and RV markets, entered the auto industry, continued to expand across the powersports, outdoor power equipment, RV, and Marine industries, and was named ABS Issuer of the Year at the 2026 GlobalCapital US Securitization Awards.

title: Lumin Digital Launches Lumin Signal, Bringing Behavioral Intelligence to Credit Unions and Banks
summary:
Lumin Digital, the Compounding Growth Platform for banks and credit unions, today announced the commercial launch of Lumin Signal, a new capability that gives financial institutions greater visibility into how retail and business users navigate the digital banking experience and the tools to act on those insights directly within the Lumin platform. 
Banks and credit unions have long had access to data showing what users do in digital banking, from logging on and paying bills to transferring funds and depositing checks.  Lumin Signal provides visibility into the experience surrounding those activities:  how users move through the platform, which features they engage with, where they abandon a process, and which capabilities are going undiscovered. Financial institutions can act on those insights directly within the digital experience and measure the impact, creating a continuous feedback loop between understanding user behavior and improving the experience.
“As digital banking plays a bigger role in the relationship between financial institutions and their users, understanding how users engage with that experience becomes increasingly important,” said Sean Weadock, Chief Product and Technology Officer at Lumin Digital. “Lumin Signal gives our clients a deeper understanding of how people are using digital banking, helping them identify opportunities to increase adoption, improve the experience, and generate more value for the capabilities they already have.”
Unlike standalone behavioral analytics tools that require extensive setup before institutions can begin collecting meaningful data, Lumin Signal is purpose-built for the Lumin platform and comes preconfigured across more than 100 pages and 700 features. Features are already tagged using banking-specific terminology, including Stop Payment, Skip-A-Pay, Remote Deposit Capture, and Positive Pay, allowing institutions to begin analyzing behavior immediately. 
Lumin Signal allows banks and credit unions to move beyond identifying friction points to resolving them directly. Key capabilities include:
Behavioral analytics: Feature adoption, session paths, funnel drop-off, and retention are tracked across the Lumin platform through pre-built dashboards that surface insights without requiring a data team or custom reporting setup. Results can be viewed across eight ready-to-use audience segments, including breakdowns by account tenure.
Guides: Admins build and publish in-app walkthroughs, tooltips, announcements, and onboarding flows directly from the Lumin Signal interface, no engineering, no integration project, no waiting on a release. A guide can go live the same day it’s conceived. For example, a single eStatement adoption guide that converts 15% of a 100,000-account paper-statement base could be worth roughly $540,000 a year.
Surveys: In-app surveys capture user feedback in context, embedded directly into the app experience at the moments that matter, without launching a separate research effort.
Because Lumin Signal runs natively within the Lumin platform, clients can add this capability without implementing and managing a separate third-party platform or vendor relationship. Lumin Signal also complements Lumin Analytics, which gives banks and credit unions individual, transaction-level visibility. While Lumin Analytics tells banks and credit unions what a specific user did, Lumin Signal tells them how the broader user base experienced it and provides them with the tools to respond. The two capabilities may be purchased independently.
For bank and credit union leaders, Lumin Signal is designed to help close a persistent measurement gap in digital banking: while adoption metrics are widely tracked, quantifying the return on investment in digital banking has remained largely ad hoc. By connecting user experience data directly to actionable steps banks and credit unions can take, Lumin Signal provides a clearer way to report progress and return on investment to executive leadership and the board.

title: UK Takes Next Step Towards First Digitally Native Government Bond
summary:
Barclays, HSBC, Lloyds, Morgan Stanley, NatWest, and RBC Capital Markets have been appointed as the Joint Lead Managers for the Digital Gilt Instrument (DIGIT) pilot issuance following a competitive procurement process.   
The appointment of Lead Managers is a key step towards the DIGIT pilot issuance, and these organisations bring expertise in both traditional sovereign bond issuance and digital markets. 
The Lead Managers will support the government by providing traditional Lead Manager services, including underwriting services, supporting investor engagement and distributing DIGIT on issuance day. 
The  DIGIT pilot, which is expected to take place by Q1 2027, will explore how distributed ledger technology (DLT) can be applied across the issuance and lifecycle of the bond. The pilot will put the new technology to the test—and show how the UK can turn its ambition for digital markets into practical action.
Lucy Rigby KC MP, Economic Secretary to the Treasury, said:
Digitalisation is central to ensuring that the UK can be a global hub for digital assets and the government’s commitment to the issuance of a digital gilt is a core part of this agenda. The appointment of Lead Managers marks an important step as we work towards issuance early next year.
DIGIT is part of the government’s wider strategy to digitalise wholesale financial markets and keep the UK competitive as distributed ledger technology changes how finance works. The Government is taking an active role in that shift, testing new infrastructure and helping create the conditions for firms to innovate and invest. 
Today’s (6 October) announcement follows the appointment of HSBC as the Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) supplier in February, and the announcement in July that HSBC and LSEG (London Stock Exchange Group) have signed a memorandum of understanding to deliver a bilateral Digital Securities Depository link.  
The six Lead Managers were chosen following a procurement process that evaluated suppliers against transparent and objective criteria, and marks another major step towards delivering on our ambitions.
The DIGIT Pilot 
DIGIT will support the government’s commitment to maintain the UK as a world-leading and global financial centre. As other financial hubs explore DLT, the potential for significant growth in this area is clear. By launching now, the government is positioning the UK financial services sector to take advantage of this opportunity. 
The pilot is seeking to: 
Enable the government to explore how DLT can be applied to UK sovereign debt issuance processes. 
Catalyse the development of UK based DLT infrastructure and the adoption of DLT across UK financial markets. 
The pilot’s design features include DIGIT being digitally native, short-dated, issued on a platform operating within the Digital Securities Sandbox (DSS), delivering on-chain settlement and independent of the government’s main debt management programme.

Economic Secretary Lucy Rigby emphasized that digitalisation is central to keeping the UK competitive as a global hub for digital assets.

title: Sapiens Launches Industry-Wide Insurance AI Maturity Index as 67% Predict Full Autonomy Within 2 to 3 Years
summary:
Sapiens International Corporation N.V. ("Sapiens") today launched the inaugural Sapiens Insurance AI Maturity Index, an international study of senior insurance professionals evaluating the current state and future ambitions of AI adoption and use across insurers of all sizes. Conducted by Research in Finance and launched at Sapiens Ignite 2026, the Index will help insurers plot their progression pathway from automation through to AI, and agentic AI adoption. Over two thirds (67%) of respondents believe AI in insurance will be fully autonomous within the next two to three years, underlining that this is an urgent priority for the whole industry. 
Only a quarter of insurers are advanced AI users
The Sapiens Insurance AI Maturity Index uses a set of criteria to place insurers in one of four categories:  Reactive, Enabled, Operational, and Autonomous. Insurers were scored on their progression in four key areas: cloud adoption, master data strategy, AI governance policy, and HR strategy and policy, with the following findings:
 Maturity Index Status
Autonomous Leaders (25%) On the cloud with some SaaS, master data and HR strategies as well as governance policy in place
Operational (28%) On the cloud with some SaaS, HR initiatives and governance policy in planning or implemented
Enabled (23%) On the cloud but not SaaS, early stages of master data strategy and governance policy with HR initiatives in planning
Reactive (24%) Early stages of cloud adoption, early stages of master data strategy, governance policy and some HR initiatives in place
“The Sapiens Insurance AI Maturity Index highlights a clear, industry-wide imperative for AI and agentic AI adoption, though insurers must accelerate their timelines or risk being left behind,” said Paul Wheeler, CEO, Sapiens. “We see firsthand what is possible when these technologies are deployed at scale, particularly with agentic AI. By implementing the right strategies today, insurers can leverage AI not just as a tool, but as a catalyst to build deeper customer trust, launch products faster, and deliver superior digital user experiences.”
Benelux and Nordics ahead of UK and North America, P&C is ahead of Life
Among the countries surveyed, Benelux (33%) and Nordics (28%) have the highest proportion of Autonomous Leaders, while the US, UK and South Africa lag with 25% 23%, and 18% respectively. 30% of P&C insurers are Autonomous Leaders, compared to only 25% of Life insurers. Understandably given their resources, leading global insurers (more than 20,000 employees) have the most Autonomous Leaders (39%). Below this are large insurers (up to 5,000 employees) of which 27% are Autonomous Leaders, and specialist or mid-sized firms (less than 1,000 employees) of which 21% are Autonomous Leaders.
Agentic AI not yet delivering benefits to the same extent as AI
Internationally, 61% of insurers say AI is a key business strategy for the future, and 51% believe it will give them a competitive advantage. The Nordics place the most importance on agentic AI and are more ready to adopt, while the UK is the lowest ranking geography for importance and adoption readiness. Autonomous Leaders are furthest ahead in their use of agentic AI in contrast to only 16% of Reactive insurers, but across all countries surveyed, more respondents say they are on average using automation (40%) and AI (42%) compared to agentic AI (24%). 
Confidence in AI high but insurers still want human oversight
Among AI and agentic AI users, 86% are very or somewhat confident in the decisions AI and agentic AI tools make, but on average 53% of agentic AI work is being checked by a human. On average, 15% of decisions made by AI or agentic AI are overridden by a human. A comparison of the country data shows the Nordics and South Africa (89%) are the most confident in their checks on agentic AI in contrast to the UK (74%) and North America (78%), yet the former countries have the most instances where they need to override more than 20% of AI decisions – South Africa (48%), Nordics (35%). This contrasts with North America (32%) and UK (29%).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
People-focused strategies to overcome AI barriers
Non-users say the biggest areas for support are governance, skills development and improving their data strategies. Autonomous Leaders place significant emphasis on upskilling their workforces (71%) compared to the international average (53%) and Reactive firms (35%). They are also moving faster to hire AI savvy talent (57%) compared to the international average (38%) and Reactive firms (20%). The Nordics also appears to be further ahead in embracing agentic AI and is mandating the use of AI for all employees (49%) compared to the UK (25%) and North America (17%).

title: Nayax Enters US Fuel Retail Through Distribution Partnership with Allied Electronics, Inc.
summary:
Nayax Ltd., a global commerce enablement, payments, and loyalty platform, today announced a distribution partnership with Allied Electronics, Inc. to bring Nayax Fuel’s VPOS Media 5 outdoor payment solution to fuel retailers across the United States. 
The US fuel market operates at exceptional scale, with convenience stores generating over $450 billion in fuel sales in 2025 and selling an estimated 80% of the fuel Americans buy, according to the National Association of Convenience Stores (NACS). Drivers increasingly pay for that fuel by card, which now represents 81% of transactions at the pump, up from 64% a decade ago. That shift has made modern payment infrastructure at the pump a necessity for US fuel retailers, central to how they serve customers. 
This partnership meets that need by bringing Nayax payment infrastructure to US fuel retailers alongside Allied, a partner retailers know and trust. Allied has served the retail petroleum industry since 1978, and its systems, including the NeXGen PRIME forecourt controller, operate at tens of thousands of locations nationwide. Nayax Fuel, a dedicated vertical within the Nayax group, extends that foundation with a comprehensive portfolio spanning payment at the dispenser, forecourt control, and station management, building on the successful integration of OTI PetroSmart and Roseman. 
“Allied and Nayax share an important focus on making the forecourt work better for retailers,” said Eli Bar, General Manager, Nayax Fuel. “Allied is one of the most respected names in US fuel retail, and our payment technology and solution give its customers a fuel-specific option built to meet the same high standard.” 
“The US fuel industry is moving through a modernization cycle, and operators need both reliable forecourt systems and modern payment solutions at the pump” said Bob Danford, Director of Engineering & Development at Allied Electronics, Inc. “Nayax complements our solutions with a purpose-built payment terminal backed by global payments infrastructure, allowing us to deliver the complete package to retailers together.” 
Nayax Fuel will present its fuel retail solutions at the NACS Show, October 7-9, 2026, at the Las Vegas Convention Center. Visitors can find Nayax at booth C6385.

title: OakNorth Selects Wise Platform to Power International Payments for UK Businesses
summary:
Wise Platform, Wise’s global payments infrastructure for banks and enterprises, has been selected by OakNorth, the digital bank for entrepreneurs, to power international payments for OakNorth’s UK business customers. 
Through the partnership, OakNorth customers - scaling businesses with annual turnover of £1 million to £100 million - will be able to make international payments instantly (77% in under 20 seconds), at the mid-market exchange rate in more than 20 currencies, including Euros, US dollars, British pounds, Indian rupees, Hong Kong dollars and Chinese yuan. The new feature gives SMEs a faster, transparent and seamless way to pay suppliers and partners around the world.
The partnership comes as UK SMEs move significant and growing volumes of money across borders. Research commissioned by Wise and independently conducted by Edgar, Dunn & Company found that UK SMEs are projected to send over £615.5 billion overseas in 2027. SME overseas payments are also forecasted to grow 22% between 2026 and 2029.
Yet as UK SMEs send more money overseas, they also stand to lose more to the hidden expenses of traditional international payments. These hidden fees are estimated to drain UK SMEs of £7.5 billion in 2027.
Manuel Sandhofer, EMEA General Manager at Wise Platform, said: "UK businesses are increasingly operating across borders, but moving money internationally can still be unnecessarily complex and expensive. For small businesses in particular, every pound lost to hidden fees is money that could otherwise be invested back into growth. Wise Platform is built to make cross-border payments fast, transparent and low-cost and we’re excited to work with OakNorth to help their customers maximise the value of every transaction they make.”
Peter King, Director of Business Banking at OakNorth, said: “Our customers are ambitious businesses with increasingly global needs and they need banking services that can keep up with the pace of their growth. Whether they’re paying suppliers overseas, entering new markets or working with international partners, knowing what their payments will cost and when their money will arrive are non-negotiable. By integrating Wise Platform, we can give our customers a better and more transparent way to move money internationally, helping them spend less time managing cross-border payments and more time focused on growing their businesses.”
Wise Platform is powered by Wise’s global payments network, with more than 80 licenses and direct access to domestic payment systems in nine markets worldwide. This infrastructure enables Wise to deliver 77% of payments instantly, in under 20 seconds. 
OakNorth joins a growing number of leading institutions in the UK and globally, including Monzo, UniCredit, N26, Morgan Stanley and Standard Chartered, using Wise Platform to enhance their international payments offering.

content: Veterans from Ramp have successfully raised $25 million in new funding for Melius, an artificial intelligence startup. Announced on Tuesday, October 6, the capital will be used to expand the Melius platform. The technology is designed to help users seamlessly create images, videos, and advertising campaigns using advanced AI tools.
content_ta: Ramp நிறுவனத்தின் முன்னாள் பணியாளர்கள் இணைந்து உருவாக்கியுள்ள AI கிரியேட்டிவ் தளமான Melius புதிய நிதியாக $25 மில்லியனை திரட்டியுள்ளது. அக்டோபர் 6 செவ்வாய்க்கிழமை அறிவிக்கப்பட்ட இந்த புதிய முதலீடு, AI மூலம் படங்கள், வீடியோக்கள் மற்றும் விளம்பரங்களை உருவாக்குவோருக்கான Melius தளத்தை விரிவுபடுத்த உதவும்.

title: Congressman Don Davis Files Bill to Prevent Federal Candidates from Trading Prediction Markets Contracts Linked to Their Elections
summary: US Representative Don Davis of North Carolina has introduced legislation intended to stop people seeking federal office from buying, selling, or holding prediction market contracts that resolve based on their own campaigns. The measure, titled the No Betting on Your Own Race Act, was filed... Read More
content: US Representative Don Davis has introduced the No Betting on Your Own Race Act in Congress. The proposed legislation aims to prevent federal candidates from buying, selling, or holding prediction market contracts that are linked to the outcome of their own election campaigns. The measure seeks to address potential conflicts of interest.
content_ta: US Representative Don Davis தனது சொந்த தேர்தல் பிரச்சாரங்களுடன் தொடர்புடைய கணிப்பு சந்தை ஒப்பந்தங்களை (prediction market contracts) federal candidates வாங்குவதைத் தடுக்கும் நோக்கில் No Betting on Your Own Race Act மசோதாவை அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளார். இந்தச் சட்டம் ஆர்லப் மோதல்களைத் தடுப்பதை நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டுள்ளது.

title: Webull Shares Plummet as House Select Committee on China Declares National Security Risk and Ties to China
summary: Webull Corporation (NASDAQ:BULL) shares are dropping today after the House Select Committee on China declared that its ties to China pose a national security risk. Currently, shares are down by around 20%. The company has a market cap of around $3.1 billion. Webull was founded... Read More
content: Shares of Webull fell sharply after the House Select Committee on China raised national security concerns regarding the company's ties to China. The drop wiped out a significant portion of its market value, reflecting growing regulatory and political scrutiny over firms with operational or ownership connections to the region.
content_ta: சீனாவுடன் தொடர்புடைய அதன் வணிக உறவுகள் தேசிய பாதுகாப்புக்கு அச்சுறுத்தலாக உள்ளதாக House Select Committee on China அறிவித்ததை அடுத்து, Webull நிறுவனத்தின் பங்குகள் கடுமையாகச் சரிந்தன. இப்பகுதி தொடர்பான நிறுவனங்கள் மீது அதிகரித்து வரும் ஒழுங்குமுறை மற்றும் அரசியல் கண்காணிப்பை இந்த வீழ்ச்சி காட்டுகிறது.

title: Third Coast to buy Oklahoma bank for $240M
summary: The announcement comes roughly a year after Houston-based Third Coast announced its $123 million purchase of Austin, Texas-based Keystone Bancshares.
content: Houston-based Third Coast has announced an agreement to acquire an Oklahoma bank for $240 million. This strategic expansion follows the company's previous $123 million acquisition of Austin, Texas-based Keystone Bancshares, which was announced approximately a year ago.
content_ta: Houston-ஐ அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்ட Third Coast நிறுவனம், Oklahoma-வைச் சேர்ந்த வங்கியை $240 மில்லியனுக்கு வாங்குவதற்கான ஒப்பந்தத்தை அறிவித்துள்ளது. இந்த நிறுவனத்தால் கடந்த ஆண்டு Austin, Texas-ஐச் சேர்ந்த Keystone Bancshares நிறுவனம் $123 மில்லியனுக்கு வாங்கப்பட்டதைத் தொடர்ந்து, தற்போது இந்த புதிய விரிவாக்க நடவடிக்கை அறிவிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: Fed consolidates bank supervision structure
summary: Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman laid out changes Tuesday to the Fed’s supervisory structure intended “to implement a culture of accountability and clear decision-making authority.”
content: The Federal Reserve announced changes to its bank supervision structure aimed at improving accountability and decision-making authority within the organization. Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman outlined the updates, which are designed to strengthen the oversight framework and foster a clearer operational culture for financial institutions regulated by the central bank.
content_ta: Fed-ன் வங்கி மேற்பார்வைக் கட்டமைப்பில் பொறுப்புக்கூறலையும் தெளிவான முடிவெடுக்கும் அதிகாரத்தையும் மேம்படுத்துவதை நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டு மாற்றங்கள் செய்யப்பட்டுள்ளதாக அறிவிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. மேற்பார்வைக்கான Vice Chair ஆன Michelle Bowman இந்த மாற்றங்களை விளக்கியுள்ளார். மத்திய வங்கியால் கட்டுப்படுத்தப்படும் நிதி நிறுவனங்களுக்கான மேற்பார்வை கட்டமைப்பை வலுப்படுத்தவும், தெளிவான செயல்பாட்டு கலாச்சாரத்தை வளர்க்கவும் இந்த மாற்றங்கள் வடிவமைக்கப்பட்டுள்ளன.

title: Payments income bolsters banks
summary: Income from card, digital and other rails has swelled to about 40% of revenue for the global bank industry, according to consulting firm McKinsey.
content: According to consulting firm McKinsey, income from card, digital, and other payment rails has grown significantly, now accounting for about 40 percent of revenue for the global banking industry. This strong expansion in payments income has helped bolster overall bank financial performance amid changing market conditions.
content_ta: McKinsey நடத்திய ஆய்வின்படி, கார்டு மற்றும் டிஜிட்டல் முறைகள் மூலம் கிடைக்கும் வருமானம் உலகளாவிய வங்கித் துறையின் ஒட்டுமொத்த வருவாயில் சுமார் 40 சதவீதமாக உயர்ந்துள்ளது. இந்த வங்கியியல் கட்டண வருவாய் வளர்ச்சி, மாறிவரும் சந்தை சூழலில் வங்கிகளின் நிதிநிலையை வலுப்படுத்த உதவியுள்ளது.

title: While America’s CLARITY Stalls, Russia’s Crypto Market Gets Official Operators
summary: Russia has registered nine crypto operators under new rules.
content: While the United States sees delays in passing clear regulatory legislation like the CLARITY Act, Russia is moving forward by officially registering several cryptocurrency market operators under new regulatory rules. This development highlights contrasting approaches to digital asset governance between the two nations, with Russia establishing formal oversight while the U.S. framework remains stalled.
content_ta: அமெரிக்காவில் CLARITY போன்ற தெளிவான ஒழுங்குமுறை சட்டங்களை இயற்றுவதில் தாமதம் ஏற்பட்டுள்ள நிலையில், ரஷ்யா புதிய விதிகளின் கீழ் பல cryptocurrency சந்தை ஆபரேட்டர்களை அதிகாரப்பூர்வமாகப் பதிவு செய்துள்ளது. இந்த நடவடிக்கை இரு நாடுகளுக்கும் இடையிலான டிஜிட்டல் சொத்து நிர்வாகத்தின் முரண்பட்ட அணுகுமுறைகளை எடுத்துக்காட்டுகிறது.

title: IOTA crypto price prediction: Can bulls reclaim $0.0572 to prevent further losses?

content_ta: IOTA-வின் விலை உயர்வு $0.060-க்கு மேல் தடைபட்டது, ஏனெனில் விற்பனையாளர்கள் டோக்கனை $0.052 நோக்கி தள்ளினர். இந்த அழுத்தம் காரணமாக வாங்குபவர்கள் ஒரு முக்கியமான ஆதரவுச் சோதனையை எதிர்கொள்கின்றனர். மேலும் விலை வீழ்ச்சியைத் தடுத்து டோக்கனை நிலைநிறுத்த bulls $0.0572 அளவை மீட்டெடுக்க முடியுமா என்பதை சந்தை பார்வையாளர்கள் உன்னிப்பாகக் கவனித்து வருகின்றனர்.

summary:

The post ICANN reveals 1,615 new domain applications, and AI suffixes like .agent and .agi are crowded appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: ICANN has revealed a massive surge with 1,615 new top-level domain applications. Among the most crowded are artificial intelligence-related suffixes such as .agent and .agi. title: Federal judge dismisses privacy lawsuit against Crypto.com over cookie tracking
summary:
